articles.title: Texas governor-elect says state will have laws to shield citizens from data centers
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 5 () - Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said on Thursday that the state will introduce laws to protect its residents with regards to data c...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said on Thursday that the state will introduce laws to protect its residents with regards to data centers, ‌citing their impact on rural communities.

With plentiful energy supplies, relatively cheap land and a ‌pro-business policy, Texas has become one of the leading regions in the world for data center developments.

"Data centers have ​moved into mostly rural communities, and there are no rules and laws to protect Texans," Democrat Hinojosa, who beat Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in Tuesday's election, told CNN in an interview.

"We will have laws to protect Texans, and we need to stop what we are doing with data ‌centers until we have those ⁠protections," she said, adding that communities should have "a seat at the table" on if and how data centers operate in their areas.

US President Donald ⁠Trump's administration has strongly backed data center expansion as a national priority, but the public is increasingly opposed to such projects, citing concerns about electricity demand, water consumption, wildlife impacts and public access ​to federal ​lands.

Abbott became one of the first Republican governors ​in the US to halt the ‌connection of new data centers to the state's electric grid and ordered a comprehensive audit of the projects.

Hinojosa has rattled the state's data center industry with a campaign pledge to halt new projects.

Billionaire Elon Musk supported Abbott in the election and had spent $158 million to promote Texas Republican US Senate candidate Ken Paxton alone, Musk said on Wednesday.

Musk's SpaceX and Tesla are headquartered ‌in the Lone Star State, where he is also ​planning a chipmaking venture.

Texas can also have a strong ​working relationship with Musk and his companies, ​but on her administration's terms, Hinojosa added.

In October, publication Texas Monthly reported ‌that the state had been discussing the ​sale of Boca Chica ​State Park to SpaceX, citing sources.

During a news conference on Thursday, Hinojosa said she had spoken to the executive director of the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission "to request ​that no action be taken" ‌while there is an ongoing transition from Abbott to her.

SpaceX did not immediately ​respond to a request for comment from Reuters.

(Reporting by Costas Pitas and Bhargav ​Acharya; Editing by Daphne Psaledakis and Christopher Cushing)

articles.title: Lula defende 'construir pontes em vez de muros' e diz que 'Brasil não é lugar para quem foge das responsabilidades' | G1
articles.standfirst: Fala ocorreu no primeiro pronunciamento em rede nacional de rádio e TV desde que presidente foi reeleito para o quarto mandato.
articles.summary: Fala ocorreu no primeiro pronunciamento em rede nacional de rádio e TV desde que presidente foi reeleito para o quarto mandato.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou neste domingo (8) que é preciso “construir pontes em vez de muros” e disse que “o Brasil não é lugar para quem foge das suas responsabilidades”. As declarações foram feitas no primeiro pronunciamento de Lula em rede nacional de rádio e TV desde que foi reeleito para o quarto mandato no dia 25 de outubro.

Lula também classificou o resultado das eleições como uma “vitória da democracia”. Segundo o presidente, o pleito teve participação recorde de eleitores e a menor abstenção dos últimos anos. De acordo com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), a taxa de abstenção de 19,2% na eleição de 2026 foi a menor registrada em uma disputa de segundo turno em 20 anos.

Lula criticou as chamadas big techs e afirmou que as empresas tentaram interferir nas eleições brasileiras pela disseminação de conteúdos com desinformação e fake news.

“Antes de ir às urnas, o povo brasileiro foi às ruas e às redes defender seus direitos, suas causas e suas esperanças. Foi a vitória da democracia”, afirmou.

"A exemplo do que vem acontecendo em alguns países pelo mundo afora, as chamadas big techs tentaram interferir no processo eleitoral brasileiro, dando milhões de visualizações a conteúdos com desinformação e fake news. Mas, com a participação popular, a verdade venceu a mentira", disse.

No discurso, Lula agradeceu os mais de 64 milhões de votos que recebeu e afirmou que vai governar para todos os brasileiros, independentemente da escolha nas urnas.

“Sou imensamente grato pelos mais de 64 milhões de votos que recebi e vou governar para todas as brasileiras e todos os brasileiros, como sempre fiz. É preciso construir pontes em vez de muros”, declarou.

Lula no primeiro pronunciamento aberto em rede de TV e rádio desde a reeleição. — Foto: Reprodução/Globoplay

Ao falar sobre o próximo mandato, Lula afirmou que pretende estruturar até o fim do ano as mudanças para o novo governo. Segundo ele, a gestão deverá ter “mais dinamismo” e ser “mais moderna”. O presidente destacou ainda a participação de jovens e idosos durante o período eleitoral e afirmou que a mobilização popular deverá continuar tendo espaço em seu próximo governo.

“É com a força da mobilização popular que vamos conduzir o governo daqui para frente, conectados com os anseios da população, ampliando a escuta e o diálogo”, disse.

No pronunciamento, Lula também enumerou propostas para o próximo mandato . Entre elas, afirmou que pretende zerar o imposto da cesta básica a partir do ano que vem e citou a proposta enviada ao Congresso para zerar a tarifa do transporte público nos fins de semana.

Lula disse ainda que o país precisa discutir “com urgência” reformas política e do Judiciário. Ao tratar da Justiça, afirmou que a magistratura precisa de “juízes isentos, éticos e livres de conflito de interesses e projetos de enriquecimento”.

O presidente também afirmou que nunca fugiu de compromissos ou críticas e fez a declaração sobre responsabilidades.

“Nunca fugi dos compromissos, nunca fugi das críticas, nunca fugi da luta e jamais abandonei meu país. O Brasil não é lugar para quem foge das suas responsabilidades.”

Na economia, Lula afirmou estar preocupado com a trajetória da dívida pública e com os juros altos e reafirmou o compromisso com a responsabilidade fiscal. Entretanto, não detalhou propostas para lidar com a questão.

"A trajetória da dívida pública e os juros altos me preocupam, por isso reafirmo meu compromisso com a responsabilidade fiscal, para viabilizar políticas sociais sustentáveis e a ampliação tão necessária do investimento. Todo esse esforço será feito preservando as regras fiscais."

Também disse que um dos objetivos do próximo governo será elevar os investimentos do país para mais de 20% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB), em parceria com o setor privado.

Durante o pronunciamento, o presidente disse que o governo terá como foco o crescimento econômico aliado às políticas sociais e defendeu investimentos em educação e em setores como economias criativa, popular, digital e verde.

"Além de acreditar na economia popular, vamos comprar a dívida das famílias junto aos bancos e perdoar a dívida dos microempreendedores individuais junto ao Governo Federal", afirmou.

Lula disse que vai colocar em prática o Prospera MEI , programa voltado aos microempreendedores que prevê perdão de dívidas, descontos sobre débitos, aumento gradual do teto de faturamento, autorização para contratar funcionários e incentivo financeiro de até R$ 5 mil.

"O Brasil caminha para ser a oitava economia do mundo com modelo de desenvolvimento que melhora a renda das famílias, cria oportunidades de crescimento através da educação e bem-estar social", afirmou.

O presidente também reforçou a intenção de abrir novos mercados internacionais e investimentos.

Na área da segurança, o presidente afirmou que, após a aprovação da PEC da Segurança Pública , encaminhará uma medida provisória para criar o Ministério da Segurança Pública . Segundo ele, o governo também pretende ampliar a integração entre as forças policiais e fortalecer o Pacto Nacional Brasil contra o Feminicídio.

"Agora, com a aprovação da PEC da Segurança Pública, encaminharei Medida Provisória para garantir a criação do Ministério da Segurança Pública", prometeu Lula.

O presidente também citou a intenção da ampliação dos mecanismos de proteção de crianças e adolescentes no ambiente digital e real.

articles.title: Veja a íntegra do pronunciamento de Lula em rede nacional de rádio e TV neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: No pronunciamento, presidente disse que se preocupa com a trajetória da dívida pública e com a taxa de juros, sem anunciar medidas nem detalhar como vai controlar os gastos do governo.
articles.summary: No pronunciamento, presidente disse que se preocupa com a trajetória da dívida pública e com a taxa de juros, sem anunciar medidas nem detalhar como vai controlar os gastos do governo.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) fez um pronunciamento em rede nacional de rádio e TV na noite deste domingo (8).

Em primeiro lugar, quero agradecer a Deus e ao povo brasileiro pela honra que me deram de governar o meu país pela quarta vez.

O Brasil viveu uma das eleições mais importantes de sua história, com a participação recorde de eleitores e a menor abstenção dos últimos anos. Antes de ir às urnas, o povo brasileiro foi às ruas e às redes defender seus direitos, suas causas e suas esperanças. Foi a vitória da democracia.

Foi emocionante ver a juventude liderar manifestações espontâneas, motivadas pelo sonho de dias melhores. Os idosos venceram distâncias e dificuldade de locomoção, e nos deram uma lição de vida: não existe limite de idade quando se trata de defender seus direitos.

O verdadeiro patriotismo nos mobilizou. Fomos às ruas uns pelos outros. Fomos às ruas pelos nossos direitos, pela nossa soberania, pela nossa natureza, pelas nossas riquezas e pelo nosso futuro.

Os filhos do Brasil não fugiram à luta. Provamos, mais uma vez, que o Brasil não cabe no quintal de ninguém.

A exemplo do que vem acontecendo em alguns países pelo mundo afora, as chamadas big techs tentaram interferir no processo eleitoral brasileiro, dando milhões de visualizações a conteúdos com desinformação e fake news. Mas, com a participação popular, a verdade venceu a mentira.

Sou imensamente grato pelos mais de 64 milhões de votos que recebi e vou governar para todas as brasileiras e todos os brasileiros, como sempre fiz. É preciso construir pontes em vez de muros.

Até o fim do ano, vou encaminhar as últimas realizações desse ciclo e estruturar as mudanças necessárias para construir o novo governo que vem pela frente. Com mais dinamismo, mais moderno e capaz de implementar, com segurança, transparência e responsabilidade, tudo o que prometemos ao povo brasileiro.

Nunca fugi dos compromissos, nunca fugi das críticas, nunca fugi da luta e jamais abandonei meu país. O Brasil não é lugar para quem foge das suas responsabilidades.

É com a força da mobilização popular que vamos conduzir o governo daqui para frente, conectados com os anseios da população, ampliando a escuta e o diálogo.

Para melhorar a vida das famílias brasileiras, zeramos o Imposto de Renda para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil, aprovamos o fim da escala 6 x 1 sem redução de salário e agora vamos zerar o imposto da cesta básica, a partir do ano que vem. Além disso, enviei ao Congresso a proposta para zerar a tarifa do transporte público aos finais de semana.

O fim das bets já está gerando impacto positivo na economia. Sem gastar em apostas, as famílias aumentaram o consumo, o comércio vende mais, a indústria produz mais, e a roda da economia volta a girar. As bets destruíram vidas e precisam ficar no passado, como o pesadelo do qual o Brasil finalmente acordou.

O Brasil precisa debater com urgência uma reforma política e do Judiciário. É dever dos agentes públicos atender esse desejo.

É chegada a hora da Justiça brasileira recuperar a sua credibilidade. A atividade da magistratura precisa de juízes isentos, éticos e livres de conflito de interesses e projetos de enriquecimento. Com uma Justiça eficaz, poderemos encarar com mais rigor a corrupção, o crime organizado e sonegadores.

O combate às facções criminosas, às milícias, aos magnatas do crime e aos agressores de mulheres e meninas depende da integração entre o Governo Federal, os estados e municípios.

Agora, com a aprovação da PEC da Segurança Pública, encaminharei Medida Provisória para garantir a criação do Ministério da Segurança Pública.

Vamos integrar e garantir a atuação enérgica de todas as forças policiais para retomar os territórios ocupados pelos criminosos e devolver a tranquilidade à população. Além disso, vamos fortalecer o Pacto Nacional Brasil contra o Feminicídio. O governo continuará implacável com os agressores.

Outro compromisso é ampliar os mecanismos de proteção para nossas crianças e adolescentes, na vida real e no ambiente digital.

O nosso trabalho terá foco no crescimento, sem abandonar o cuidado com quem mais precisa, sobretudo os idosos. Iremos aprofundar a política nacional de cuidados. A população brasileira está envelhecendo, e é urgente um aperfeiçoamento das políticas públicas, para que sejam capazes de promover qualidade de vida e dignidade para a população idosa.

O Brasil caminha para ser a oitava economia do mundo com modelo de desenvolvimento que melhora a renda das famílias, cria oportunidades de crescimento através da educação e bem-estar social.

Nenhum desenvolvimento é possível sem uma revolução no nosso modelo de ensino. É por isso que iremos universalizar a educação integral e o Pé-de-Meia. Criaremos o Pé-de-Meia Universitário e seguiremos investindo no ensino técnico, na educação digital e nas universidades.

A economia brasileira tem prosperado, o desemprego está baixo, a inflação sob controle e a renda do trabalhador está crescendo.

A trajetória da dívida pública e os juros altos me preocupam, por isso reafirmo meu compromisso com a responsabilidade fiscal, para viabilizar políticas sociais sustentáveis e a ampliação tão necessária do investimento. Todo esse esforço será feito preservando as regras fiscais.

Um dos principais objetivos do nosso governo é elevar o investimento do país para mais de 20% do PIB, em parceria com o setor privado. Para tanto, vamos criar as condições para reduzir a taxa de juros.

Além de acreditar na economia popular, vamos comprar a dívida das famílias junto aos bancos e perdoar a dívida dos microempreendedores individuais junto ao Governo Federal.

Iremos colocar em prática o Prospera MEI, com um conjunto de medidas para impulsionar os pequenos negócios. Estamos prontos para o desafio de gerar empregos de mais qualidade, principalmente para os jovens.

Com abertura de novos mercados internacionais e investimentos em uma nova indústria nacional, vamos fortalecer setores estratégicos da economia, a exemplo da economia criativa, a economia digital e a economia verde.

Não perderemos a oportunidade de fazer do Brasil um país capaz de transformar nossas riquezas naturais em um futuro de oportunidades para os nossos trabalhadores e empreendedores, e em crescimento para a nossa nação.

Com fé e esperança, seguiremos construindo um Brasil mais humanista, solidário e fraterno. Um Brasil melhor e mais próspero para todas as pessoas.

Muito obrigado, e que Deus abençoe o Brasil e o povo brasileiro.

articles.title: El choque entre Rufián y Albiol por la inmigración en Badalona: “Tú eres más pobre por culpa del negro"
articles.standfirst: El portavoz de ERC estuvo en un evento de precampaña en Badalona y mandó una serie de palabras dirigidas hacia el alcalde de la ciudad
articles.summary: El portavoz de ERC estuvo en un evento de precampaña en Badalona y mandó una serie de palabras dirigidas hacia el alcalde de la ciudad
articles.body: Las elecciones generales del próximo domingo, 29 de noviembre, siguen estando en pleno foco de actualidad. Los diferentes partidos políticos siguen con sus actos de precampaña a lo largo de toda la geografía nacional. En este contexto, este domingo, 8 de noviembre, Gabriel Rufián, portavoz de ERC, estuvo en Badalona en un evento de esta índole. El político mandó un mensaje tajante hacia el alcalde de Badalona, Xavier García Albiol. En primer lugar, quiso criticar el discurso del edil sobre la okupación de viviendas y cuestionó que se responsabilice a la inmigración de los problemas económicos de la ciudadanía: “Aquí gobierna un señor que es muy hábil, como prácticamente todos los fascistas. La gente normal está mucho más cerca de ser desahuciada por un banco que de que le ocupen su piso”. “Pero es igual. Es igual decir que uno es pobre u otro precario (…) Tú eres más pobre por culpa del negro, de la mujer o del que acaba de llegar a los pisos de un camión. Es miserable. Nosotros somos conscientes, es un reto. Es un reto que debe afrontarse desde la inclusión, la convivencia y los derechos y las obligaciones. No somos menos de izquierdas, somos más útiles”, sentenció Rufián en un vídeo difundido en su cuenta personal de la red social X. Xavier García Albiol citó el tuit del portavoz de ERC al Congreso y se pronunció en los siguientes términos: “Veo que hoy Rufián ha venido a Badalona a insultarme porque me niego a que mi ciudad asuma las consecuencias de la inmigración ilegal”. “Si tanta solidaridad tiene, es muy fácil: que acojan en los propios ayuntamientos de ERC y del PSC a todos los que dejan entrar sin control. Fin del problema”, culminó el alcalde de Badalona.

articles.title: Deputy White House Chief of Staff Richard Walters exits job ahead of Stephen Miller takeover
articles.summary: Stephen Miller praised Richard Walters as an “invaluable member" who will continue helping the administration from outside the White House.
articles.body:
White House Deputy Chief of Staff Richard Walters, a longtime ally of outgoing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, is leaving the Trump administration following President Donald Trump's decision to replace Wiles with Stephen Miller.

Miller confirmed Walters' departure in a statement to Fox News, describing him as an "invaluable member" of the White House who will continue to assist the administration from the outside.

"Richard has been an invaluable member of the White House and has helped deliver some of the Administration's biggest victories. While he will be leaving us, Richard will continue to help from the outside as we continue to work with all of our strength to deliver for President Trump and his courageous fight to Save America," Miller said.

The move ends Walters' months-long tenure in the role, which he was appointed to in May 2026, according to LegiStorm. Walters previously served as executive director of the inaugural committee for Trump and Vice President JD Vance, according to Georgetown University, where he was a fellow at the Institute of Politics and Public Service.

The departure marks the first major staff turnover as Miller prepares to install his own leadership team when he takes over Monday. The move is part of a broader effort by Trump to overhaul his administration following the midterm elections , in which Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate.

Miller's wife, Katie, on Sunday also announced that she would stop recording new episodes of her show, The Katie Miller Podcast, where she interviews political figures, athletes and other public personalities.

She said the decision was based on what was best for her children and family as her husband's new role brings a shift in priorities.

"With @StephenM taking on this new role for President Trump, I've decided to stop recording new podcast episodes," Katie said in a post on X.

"Nothing is more important than raising our four kids. While I've loved the podcast, the time commitment is too great and now is the time to step away. I'll be cheering President Trump and his team on from outside the administration," she added.

Katie said the podcast will release two more episodes that were recorded before her decision.

Trump named Miller as his new chief of staff Friday, calling him one of his "most trusted advisors."

A White House official told Fox News Digital the decision was also "very amicable" and Wiles handed in her resignation Thursday night.

articles.title: Former RFK Jr. adviser accuses Trump officials of corruption
articles.summary: Calley Means, a White House senior adviser and aide to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who resigned last month, said on "Face the Nation with Margare...
articles.body:
The full transcript of Margaret Brennan's interview with Calley Means is available on cbsnews.com.

A former senior White House adviser and top aide to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is accusing several Trump administration officials, including the recently resigned White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, of prioritizing industry interests over the health of voters as part of the White House's midterm elections strategy.

"Underneath Trump's nose, in many cases, you had a group of former lobbyists, catering to the vaping industry, catering to the ultra-processed food industry, catering to the pharmaceutical industry, catering to the pesticide industry and doing their bidding with an excuse that we need their money for the midterms and really need to actually go against what voters said," Calley Means told "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan in an interview that aired Sunday.

Means helped found the "Make America Healthy Again" movement and helped form the winning alliance between Mr. Trump and Kennedy in 2024 before serving as Kennedy's top aide. Means helped lead the Department of Health and Human Services' efforts to revise the country's dietary guidelines and remove soda and candy from SNAP benefits before resigning last month.

He told CBS News that Wiles and "a very close-knit crew" of other White House advisers "were taking money from the industries we ran on fighting against."

Means went public Friday with very specific allegations of corruption against Wiles and a call for President Trump to "clear his house" in an interview he taped Thursday for "The Joe Rogan Experience" podcast.

He claimed Wiles and her deputy, James Blair, relentlessly pushed HHS to find a pathway to approve fruit-flavored vapes. In early May, the Food and Drug Administration approved some fruit-flavored e-cigarettes.

Blair denied Means' characterization of his role in the vape debate in a statement to CBS News.

"I didn't promote flavored vaping specifically at all," Blair said. "I was tasked with driving FDA to make its process for approving or denying nicotine delivery device applications work the way current federal law dictates it works, which is that applicants get a yes or no answer on approval in six months. Calley is intentionally misrepresenting my role and my responsibility because he opposes the issue entirely. Even though the president himself has made his position on smoking and smoking alternatives known very publicly and has provided clear direction. Calley just doesn't like it."

Two sources familiar with the process told CBS News that Blair was tasked by Mr. Trump with driving then-FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary to more quickly respond to applications from the nicotine industry, but also acknowledged that the president sought to make flavored vapes more available.

As a 2024 presidential candidate, Mr. Trump vowed to "save" vaping and mentioned his past efforts on behalf of flavored vaping during his first administration, which he said in a social media post was intended to get people off smoking. Mr. Trump won backing from e-cigarette companies, shop owners and vaping enthusiasts.

In May, Makary was pressed to resign his post as FDA commissioner amid reports that he had been pressured by the White House to approve the fruit-flavored vapes.

"Big tobacco exploited their connections to administration and HHS officials to put repeated pressure on me to approve fruit-flavored vapes that appeal to children—I wouldn't do it," Makary said in a statement to CBS News. "The Kratom/7-OH lobby ran the same playbook to undermine my efforts to make this new 'gas station heroin' illegal. As FDA commissioner, I always rejected political corruption just as voters across the political spectrum did last week."

Multiple sources confirmed to CBS News the New York Times' reporting in May that tobacco lobbyists had been at the president's Florida golf course with him at lunch and pushed him on the way e-cigarettes were being regulated by the FDA. Means claimed Wiles set up the meeting.

Wiles submitted her resignation to Mr. Trump on Thursday night, a U.S. official and a senior White House adviser told CBS News. Her resignation was tied to Republicans' midterm defeats , according to three sources familiar with the matter. The departure became public shortly after Mr. Trump taped an interview with 60 Minutes midday Friday.

When asked if it was his intention to get Wiles removed from her position, Means responded, "Yes. I think President Trump has been subverted by people that are beholden to special interests and not what President Trump ran on, and what voters voted for." It is not clear at this time whether the public remarks factored into the president's decision to expedite Wiles' departure.

In a statement to CBS News, Wiles denied Means' allegations that she arranged for tobacco industry representatives to meet with the president at his golf course to discuss vape policy.

Earlier this year, Mr. Trump signed an executive order to boost production of glyphosate, a herbicide that is included in the weedkiller Roundup and which has been found to be linked to cancer. WHO has deemed glyphosate to be "probably carcinogenic to humans."

For decades as a private attorney, Kennedy had spearheaded a legal challenge to the chemical giant Monsanto for its use of the herbicide. In a statement on social media at the time of the president's order, Kennedy said: "Our agricultural system depends heavily on these chemicals."

Kennedy testified to Congress in March that he was "very clear with the president about my own displeasure with the executive order." Kennedy said in that testimony the executive order on glyphosate "came from the Pentagon," and "the president felt it was necessary for national security reasons."

In June, the Supreme Court sided with Monsanto, ruling that it cannot be held liable for failing to warn consumers about alleged cancer risks in Roundup. On "Face the Nation," Means accused White House adviser Heidi Overton of working with the Department of Justice to write a brief to the Supreme Court, urging them to take the case prior to Mr. Trump's executive order.

A senior White House official told CBS News that the solicitor general wrote the brief for the Supreme Court at the request of the court. The official also said that Dr. Overton did weigh in on the brief in the final stages but just made changes to "tone." The Trump administration argued in court filings that federal standards supersede state-level liability claims, which was the same position taken by glyphosate-maker Monsanto, now known as Bayer.

There is an ongoing EPA review of glyphosate, expected to conclude in early 2027. Means alleged the prior EPA review of glyphosate was "thrown out because it had ghostwritten research showing Bayer bribed EPA officials."

Means resigned last month and said he is leaving "with tremendous respect for President Trump and Robert F. Kennedy Jr."

Food stocks rallied on the day of his departure. Means told "Face the Nation" that he was frustrated with his stalled efforts to create a federal definition of ultra-processed food, which he argues is poisoning American children.

"There was relentless lobbying against this because the industry and they said this in meetings with me and other people, they just don't want a definition because they don't want Americans to have more transparency into what they're eating because there's a shift away from ultra-processed food right now."

Means said on "Face the Nation" that he is confident of Mr. Trump's stance on the "issue of improving health for children," but claimed that the president's advisers gave him poor advice and "treated him like a baby in many respects and used him."

"They would block access to and information to him all the time," Means alleged. "I would be not surprised at all, you know, if they had very short conversations on these issues, you know, where the president's extremely busy and the president said, 'OK, whatever.'"

Mr. Trump's top adviser Stephen Miller , who is set to take over the White House chief of staff role on Monday, wasn't among them, according to Means.

"Stephen Miller wants to get transformative things done with Bobby Kennedy and President Trump that are not partisan, but structural," he said. "He wants to get the same things done that Elizabeth Warren and (Abdul) El-Sayed and other people are running on. And I think there is a major opportunity to come together and get some big things done, which, quite frankly, we have to do."

In August, Mr. Trump nominated policy aide Dr. Heidi Overton to be the next FDA commissioner. Kennedy has endorsed Overton's nomination.

However, Means told CBS News that Overton "was the biggest block to MAHA policies I encountered in the government," alleging she "did whatever" Wiles "told her to do."

Means alleged that in one particular meeting, Overton told Makary — whom Means described as Overton's "mentor" — that she "couldn't help" him on other policies unless he approved "a drug that he thought scientifically should not be approved," Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine, mFLUSIVA.

In August, the FDA approved mFLUSIVA for adults ages 50 and older. It was the first influenza vaccine using mRNA technology to receive FDA approval.

The approval came despite repeated criticism of mRNA technology by Kennedy, who in 2025 canceled 22 vaccine development projects that use mRNA technology. The FDA had earlier this year said it would refuse to consider Moderna's application. But it reversed course about a week later. Clinical trials found mFLUSIVA to be slightly more effective than the standard flu shot.

"It's just a factual statement that after Marty left, partly due to the vaping issue, she drove the creation of the relaxed vaping strategy," Means said, adding that he does not believe Overton has the "character or integrity" to be FDA commissioner.

A spokesman for Overton responded to Means' criticism of her qualifications and told CBS News that "two former FDA commissioners think otherwise."

Calley Means is the brother of Dr. Casey Means, also a close ally of Kennedy. CBS News previously reported that both played a key role in coordinating Kennedy's endorsement of Mr. Trump during the 2024 presidential campaign. Casey Means was briefly Mr. Trump's pick for surgeon general, but her name was withdrawn in April because her bid stalled in the Senate.

articles.title: US chipmaker Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair
articles.summary: Huang has confirmed he had been having an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.
articles.body:
United States-based chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its chief executive officer, billionaire Jensen Huang, after he confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence.

In an announcement on Sunday, Nvidia said the probe would be conducted by a “committee of independent directors” with outside counsel.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board of directors said.

It said the board continued to have “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team”. Huang will continue to lead Nvidia during the probe.

The investigation follows a report in The New York Times last month that Jensen may have been the target of a Chinese espionage plot.

China and the US have been in competition to dominate key tech sectors like artificial intelligence (AI).

Amid the AI boom, Nvidia has seen demand for its chips and programming interfaces explode, resulting in the company being valued in the trillions of dollars.

For years, the US has sought to restrict the export of advanced chips to China, fearing the Asian superpower could gain an edge over its technology and military sectors.

But on October 29, The New York Times said it had obtained exclusive information that a Chinese woman named Alice Huang, or Huang Le, sought to cultivate close ties with Jensen Huang in an effort to glean information about Nvidia’s technology.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, has denied any allegations of spying in the case.

The New York Times also reported that Alice Huang’s employer, Megaspeed, had become one of Nvidia’s largest buyers, purchasing some $4.8bn in equipment from the US firm.

Jensen Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, who is of no relation, spurred fierce bipartisan backlash in the US Congress in the aftermath of the report.

“For months, bipartisan members of Congress have raised concerns about NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips going to China,” Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote in a statement.

“NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers. And we need to pass bipartisan legislation we have ready to stop advanced American technology from going to China.”

Republican lawmakers in the House of Representatives also called on Huang to appear and testify before Congress about the affair on November 18.

“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” Republicans John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford said in a statement.

In an email to Nvidia staff on Sunday, Huang had admitted to having an extramarital relationship.

“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse ‌for what I did,” Huang said.

Nvidia has grown rapidly in recent years with the rise of AI, producing chips for large language models developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google.

Huang has also been closely working with US President Donald Trump since the Republican leader returned to office in 2025.

In August of that year, the Trump administration announced it would take a 15 percent cut of certain Nvidia chip sales to China.

Trump reportedly bought as much as $1.6m in Nvidia stock and sold about $1m in August, ahead of November’s midterm elections.

After the midterm races last Tuesday, stocks for AI-related companies, including Nvidia, tumbled in reaction to widespread Republican losses.

Trump has pushed back against calls to regulate AI companies, but many Democrats during the midterms campaigned on placing restrictions on the companies, including on the construction of data centres.

Nvidia lost $450bn in market value in a single trading day last week, but it rebounded on Friday, regaining 4 percent of its losses.

When asked by reporters if Huang would accompany him to November’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China, Trump was noncommittal.

“I don’t know, but I’d certainly take him,” Trump replied from the tarmac in West Palm Beach, Florida. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong. He dealt with somebody, but so does everybody else.”

He added that Huang was a “fine person” and has done an “amazing job for our country”.

“I think he’s an honourable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it,” Trump said of the speculation about Huang’s behaviour.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Austin home targeted by well-funded leftist groups aboard party buses
articles.summary: Three far-left nonprofits with $56.1 million in combined revenue organized a theatrical protest outside Elon Musk's Austin-area home
articles.body: Three far-left nonprofits with combined annual revenues of $56.1 million escalated their protests against SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk this week by targeting his Austin-area home with a seemingly innocuous post-election "party" featuring two chartered buses, music, speeches, theatrical Cybertruck piñatas and dancing to Queen’s "We Will Rock You." The event’s organizers – VOCAL-TX, the fiscally-sponsored project of a New York 501(c)(3) nonprofit; the Center for Popular Democracy Inc., a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Brooklyn; and People’s Action, a 501(c)(4) political nonprofit based in Chicago – framed the Saturday event as a tame "People Over Billionaires Election After Party." The demonstration reflected growing coordination among leftist networks worldwide, from Paris to Portland, Ore., supplying organizers, transportation, coalition partners, event platforms, messaging and other logistical support for actions presented as "grassroots." As Democratic politicians threaten investigations into Trump’s corporate backers, including Musk, the street protests help create the appearance of bottom-up support. The leaders of the organizations behind the "After Party," held in West Lake Hills, Tex., where Musk owns a sprawling home, didn’t provide comment in response to queries from Fox News Digital, but they have insisted in the past that their local protests are the result of "organic" organizing in communities. A now-ubiquitous, mass-produced anti-Musk "I AM STEALING FROM YOU" poster, featuring the tech billionaire with creepy eyes, has appeared at demonstrations nationwide and was also on display at the Austin protest outside his home. WHO’S FUNDING AMERICA’S PROTEST UNREST? FOX NATION'S NEW 'RIOT INC.' FOLLOWS THE MONEY TO FIND OUT This weekend’s organizers helped lead the "Tesla Takedown" protests that sometimes turned ugly last year. According to a Fox News Digital investigation, 258 organizations with combined annual revenues of an estimated $2.6 billion were behind those protests. At Saturday’s event, participants arrived at the property in two blue Fly-Rides party buses and additional vehicles. Organizers blasted music including Queen’s "We Will Rock You," over loudspeakers. "We'll bring the music, you bring the dance moves! This is family friendly, peaceful and FUN event!" the organizers wrote, promoting the event. The Austin American-Statesman covered the event and cast it playfully, with the headline "Dozens party outside Elon Musk's West Lake Hills home after campaign donations fell flat." It wrote about how organizers led a "Love Train" conga line and distributed party hats and refreshments, including cider. The organizations behind the campaign are veterans of the professional protest industry. While this event was peaceful, the rhetoric of demonization and polarization at protests causes researchers at organizations like the Network Contagion Research Institute to conclude that that they can create a "permission structure" for political violence. ‘ASTROTURF’: CRITICS SPECULATE TESLA PROTESTS ARE NOT A GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT, BUT A CAREFULLY ORGANIZED CAMPAIGN The three nonprofits behind this weekend’s protests are part of a powerful national tax-exempt nonprofit industry that has increasingly taken to the streets over the past decade in coordinated, orchestrated campaigns in local communities, creating the image of homegrown organic demonstrations. The three groups reported $56.1 million in combined 2024 revenue, according to their most recent tax filings. Organizers promoted the event as a peaceful celebration of voters rejecting the influence of wealthy donors. About 60 people attended, according to estimates. The demonstration followed in the spirit of the very coordinated "Tesla Takedown" protests launched at Texas dealerships in early 2025, when activists organized demonstrations against Tesla and Musk over his political activities and role in the new Trump administration and the Department of Government Efficiency, called DOGE. Those protests led to vandalism against Tesla vehicles and dealerships. A wider network of openly pro-communist groups, including Freedom Road Socialist Organization, carried posters with messages like "DOWN WITH BILLIONAIRES. WE NEED SOCIALISM." Congressional lawmakers and Justice Department prosecutors are investigating an American-born, Shanghai-based tycoon, Neville Roy Singham, for funding and backing pro-communist groups. Some of those groups, including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, ANSWER Coalition, CodePink and People's Forum, have supported the regular protests that have hit America's streets, including the anti-Musk demonstrations. . DEMOCRATS SET SIGHTS ON ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER MIDTERM WINS, BUT PRITZKER DRAWS A SURPRISING LINE Much like the networks behind "No Kings," "Hands Off," "ICE Out" and other protests over the past year, the financial filings of the organizations behind this weekend’s demonstration show the scale of the infrastructure behind these groups. The Center for Popular Democracy reported $40.9 million in 2024 revenue. People’s Action Institute reported $2.1 million, and Voices of Community Activists and Leaders Inc., or VOCAL-NY, which fiscally sponsors VOCAL-TX, reported $13.1 million. The organizations are separate entities, and the figures don’t represent a shared operating budget. VOCAL-TX’s donation page identifies VOCAL-NY as its 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor and sister organization. VOCAL-NY describes the organization as a statewide grassroots membership group focused on "building the power of low-income people" impacted by "HIV/AIDS, drug policy, mass incarceration, the war on drugs and homelessness." It says its work is "accomplished through community organizing, campaigns & harm reduction services." The Center for Popular Democracy Inc. lists VOCAL-TX among its affiliates and describes itself as a network of "grassroots" organizations operating across dozens of states, building a "representative, multiracial society and government where all thrive, no exceptions," according to its nonprofit mission statement. SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN The Center for Popular Democracy reported $38.2 million in contributions and $14.6 million in other salaries and compensation in 2024. Its two co-executive directors received an average total compensation of $234,026, including bonuses in 2024, according to their latest tax filings, about four times more than the $63,360 median annual earnings of full-time, year-round U.S. workers that year. VOCAL-NY reported nearly $3.5 million in other salaries and wages and listed its Texas co-director among its highest-paid employees, earning $113,842 in salary and $21,854 in bonuses in 2024. People’s Action describes itself as a national network of grassroots groups "organized to promote economic, racial and social equity through national, regional and local advocacy campaigns." Saturday’s gathering transformed a political victory "party" into a theatrical public spectacle, using buses, coordinated messaging, music and symbolic props to deliver a broader message: that billionaire wealth shouldn’t determine the direction of American politics. Protesters didn't specifically address the millionaires and billionaires that funnel money to Democratic politicians such as George Soros, Reid Hoffman and Pierre Omidyar, to name just a few. Participants carried signs reading "Texas is not for sale" and "Alright Texas! Now let’s tax Musk." Attendees also smashed star-shaped and piñatas shaped like a Tesla Cybertruck. CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE Eli Cortez, a VOCAL-TX bus captain, told attendees that the event was intended to celebrate voters rejecting the political influence of billionaires, according to coverage by the Austin American-Statesman. Cortez didn’t respond to a request for comment. The demonstration focused on Musk’s spending during the 2026 election cycle. A New York Times analysis placed Musk’s total disclosed political spending at approximately $474 million, while other analyses based more narrowly on Federal Election Commission filings put the figure at roughly $445 million. About $212 million supported Texas Republican Ken Paxton’s unsuccessful Senate campaign through allied political committees. May Day Strong, another far-left coalition tagged in the social media promotion of the event, describes itself as a "constellation" of more than 600 labor and community organizations, many of them socialist and communist. Its stated demands include taxing the rich, opposing ICE, expanding "democracy" and organizing workers to "protest, refuse to comply, and take the economic actions" needed to oppose the Trump administration. Austin protesters carried a trademark poster with a creepy image of Musk and the message, "I Am Stealing From You," now a mainstay at protests, not as a spontaneous grassroots creation but a strategic asset. The Progressive Change Institute, the 501(c)(3) sister organization of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee, has taken credit for commissioning the art early last year by Washington, D.C., political street artist Absurdly Well. The graphic became part of the propaganda of the broader "Hands Off" protest network, which distributed thousands of copies of the poster. CNN, the Associated Press, the New York Times, Axios, TIME, Reuters, The Hill and MSNBC host Rachel Maddow have splashed photos of the poster in its coverage Progressive Change Campaign Committee's online member engagement director has said the merchandise was intended to serve an organizing purpose beyond fundraising, with the goal of making Elon Musk "a real liability for the administration." The group now gives donors "5- or 10-pack of anti-Elon Musk rally posters" in exchange for donations: $135 for a five-pack, $250 for a $10-pack and $30 for a single poster. At least two of the iconic posters landed in the "party" protest outside Musk's home, held overhead by demonstrators. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Trump says 'only kidding' about naming UFC CEO as White House press secretary
articles.summary: By Jarrett Renshaw and David Lawder WEST PALM BEACH, Nov 8 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump on Sunday said he was "only kidding" when he suggested UFC CEO...
articles.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Nov 8 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump on Sunday said he ‌was "only kidding" when he suggested UFC CEO Dana White ‌could become his next White House press secretary, after a social media ​post a day earlier stirred speculation about recruiting his feisty ally and signaled a combative approach to dealing with Democrats as they prepare to take control of Congress.

Trump said White, a prominent ‌supporter, "loves the idea" ⁠of taking the job but insisted he had not been serious about the prospect, describing the ⁠suggestion as "just a little fun."

"I will tell you, I was only kidding," Trump told reporters, explaining that he had posted photographs ​of prominent ​UFC fighters as potential assistants ​to White as part of ‌the joke.

In Saturday's post, Trump described White as a "violent Fighter and Warrior" and suggested he bring several current or former UFC champions to serve as assistants, saying they were needed to "defend us against the Lunatic Left."

Trump said White would visit ‌him at the White House on ​Monday, but added that the meeting ​was planned for other ​reasons.

White, who has led the Ultimate Fighting Championship ‌for more than two decades, has ​been a ​close Trump ally and helped mobilize support for his 2024 presidential campaign.

He has also appeared alongside Trump at several ​political events and ‌helped bring UFC fights to the White House lawn ​this year.

(Reporting by David Lawder, Costas Pitas and Jarrett ​Renshaw, editing by Michelle Nichols)

articles.title: Traição, espionagem e investigação: entenda o caso que expõe a Nvidia e seu CEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa, considerada central na corrida pelo desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial, abriu investigação contra o seu fundador, Jensen Huang, após reportagens apontarem suspeitas de espionagem chinesa. Ele diz que vai colaborar com as apurações.
articles.summary: Empresa, considerada central na corrida pelo desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial, abriu investigação contra o seu fundador, Jensen Huang, após reportagens apontarem suspeitas de espionagem chinesa. Ele diz que vai colaborar com as apurações.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante evento em Washington — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo

O fundador e CEO da Nvidia , Jensen Huang , admitiu ter sido infiel à esposa em meio a suspeitas de que foi alvo de espionagem. A empresa anunciou neste domingo (8) que abriu uma investigação independente para apurar se ele foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência de outro país.

O caso deve aumentar a pressão sobre a Nvidia num momento em que investidores já recuam diante das dúvidas sobre a sustentabilidade do mercado de inteligência artificial. As ações da fabricante de chips sofreram fortes quedas recentemente, e o episódio também pode levantar questionamentos sobre o futuro de Huang no comando da companhia.

A empresa é considerada central na corrida global pelo desenvolvimento da IA, com chips que alimentam muitos dos data centers e sistemas de computação usados para treinar e operar modelos da tecnologia. Seus processadores avançados também estão no centro das restrições de exportação impostas pelos Estados Unidos para limitar o acesso da China a semicondutores de ponta.

O caso envolve ainda uma executiva ligada à China e suspeitas sobre a cadeia de chips de IA. Veja o que se sabe até agora:

Em mensagem enviada aos funcionários da Nvidia, obtida pela Reuters, o executivo confirmou o relacionamento extraconjugal e assumiu "total responsabilidade" por seus atos.

"Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações fizeram mal a ela e aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz", escreveu Huang.

Dirigindo-se a colegas, ao conselho de administração, aos parceiros e aos acionistas, ele afirmou que está comprometido com a empresa. "Minha responsabilidade é servir a vocês e ser digno da confiança de vocês. Não estive à altura dessa responsabilidade", escreveu.

➡️ Imigrante taiwanês, Jen-Hsun Huang, hoje conhecido como Jensen Huang, tem 63 anos e fundou a Nvidia em 1993 com dois sócios. Antes de dominar os chips de IA, a empresa era dedicada a placas de vídeo, que melhoram a qualidade dos gráficos em jogos e vídeos. No início de outubro, a fortuna de Huang ultrapassou US$ 200 bilhões (cerca de R$ 1 trilhão), segundo estimativas da revista Forbes.

Segundo a Nvidia, Huang permanecerá no cargo de CEO da empresa durante a investigação.

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante conferência da empresa em 17 de março de 2026 — Foto: Reuters/Carlos Barria

Segundo uma reportagem do jornal The New York Times, publicada em outubro, Huang teve um relacionamento com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura.

Autoridades dos EUA investigaram a executiva e concluíram que ela atuava como agente da inteligência chinesa.

Alice Huang trabalhou anteriormente como repórter de televisão na China antes de se tornar uma das principais executivas da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura que se tornou uma das maiores clientes da Nvidia no Sudeste Asiático. Segundo o NYT, a Megaspeed comprou mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em chips da Nvidia nos últimos dois anos.

A própria Megaspeed foi investigada por autoridades americanas, por suspeitas de que tenha ajudado Pequim a obter acesso a chips avançados de IA, cuja exportação para a China é proibida.

➡️ Desde 2022, os Estados Unidos mantêm controles de exportação destinados a restringir o acesso da China aos chips avançados da Nvidia e aos equipamentos necessários para produzi-los.

A carta do CEO da Nvidia aos funcionários não mencionou Alice Huang nem tratou de suas aparentes ligações com Pequim.

Huang, no entanto, fez referência às preocupações de segurança nacional levantadas pelas reportagens e afirmou que apoia a investigação do conselho e que cooperará integralmente com a apuração.

Anteriormente, no fim de outubro, o CEO havia dito à Bloomberg News que sua relação e suas interações com Alice Huang eram "completamente normais e nada incomuns".

A Megaspeed informou que sua atual liderança leva o assunto a sério e contratou advogados externos para conduzir uma investigação interna. Alice Huang não respondeu aos pedidos de comentário.

A Nvidia é uma das maiores fabricantes de chips do mundo e, no final de outubro, virou a primeira da história a atingir US$ 5 trilhões em valor de mercado.

➡️ Seus chips são usados para treinar modelos de inteligência artificial, como o do ChatGPT, que exigem muita capacidade computacional, e entre os clientes estão praticamente todas as gigantes da tecnologia, como Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta e Spotify.

Por isso, a investigação deve aumentar a pressão sobre a empresa num momento em que investidores já recuam diante das dúvidas sobre a sustentabilidade do setor de IA.

As ações perderam todos os ganhos acumulados neste ano, segundo a Reuters, em meio a uma queda mais ampla do setor de tecnologia provocada por preocupações com o futuro da inteligência artificial.

➡️ As ações de big techs derreteram após as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA. Um dos motivos é a vitória do Partido Democrata, que aumentou a preocupação de que o setor de tecnologia enfrente mais resistência para construir centros de dados, instalações que consomem grandes quantidades de energia e água.

O caso também pode levantar questionamentos sobre o futuro de Huang no comando da companhia que ele ajudou a fundar.

"Há claramente o risco de Jensen ser afastado do cargo de CEO, dependendo do resultado da investigação do conselho, e isso aumentará a pressão sobre as ações, já que ele é muito importante para a história e a estratégia global da Nvidia”, afirmou Dan Ives, sócio e diretor-gerente sênior da Yorkville Ives & Co.

O jornal afirma que Donald Trump foi informado sobre as suspeitas há cerca de um ano, mas não tomou nenhuma medida, pois integrantes do governo temiam que uma reação prejudicasse os negócios da Nvidia e complicasse as relações entre os dois países.

Em outra reportagem, publicada também neste domingo, o NYT diz que o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, supervisionou um memorando altamente confidencial que alertava autoridades de alto escalão do governo sobre o relacionamento de Huang.

A Casa Branca, a Agência Central de Inteligência (CIA) e a Agência de Segurança Nacional (NSA) se recusaram a comentar o caso.

Questionado neste domingo, Trump afirmou que ainda não conversou com Huang sobre o assunto, mas que considera o CEO “uma boa pessoa”.

“Acho que ele é um cara honrado”, disse a jornalistas, acrescentando que Huang “fez um trabalho incrível pelo nosso país”. Sobre as acusações, Trump afirmou que Huang “provavelmente tem uma explicação” e que é necessário ouvi-lo.

Ilustração mostra o logotipo da NVIDIA e a placa-mãe do computador — Foto: REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Ilustração

Segundo a Nvidia, "um comitê de diretores independentes, com o auxílio de assessoria jurídica externa e independente, supervisionará a investigação".

A companhia disse que o conselho não tem motivos para acreditar que a segurança nacional dos EUA ou informações confidenciais da empresa tenham sido comprometidas, mas que a apuração analisará todas as informações disponíveis.

Huang apoia integralmente o processo e se comprometeu a colaborar. Um porta-voz afirmou que ele está comprometido em continuar à frente da Nvidia como CEO, sem interrupções.

Parlamentares republicanos de alto escalão da Câmara dos Representantes dos EUA pediram que Huang preste esclarecimentos ao Congresso ainda neste mês.

articles.title: RS voltará a atrasar salários? Entenda polêmica para 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Deputados ligados ao governador eleito Luciano Zucco afirmam que o Rio Grande do Sul pode voltar a atrasar salários de servidores em 2027. A gestão atual, comandada por Eduardo Leite, nega.
articles.summary: Aliados do governador eleito do RS, Luciano Zucco, afirmam que o déficit no estado será maior dos que os R$ 4,8 bilhões negativos apresentados pela gestão Eduardo Leite.
articles.body:
Luciano Zucco (PL) e Eduardo Leite (PSD) — Foto: Mateus Raugust/Divulgação

Existe a possibilidade de o Rio Grande do Sul voltar a atrasar o salário dos servidores públicos a partir de 2027, segundo deputados estaduais ligados ao governo eleito de Luciano Zucco ( PL ). A atual gestão, de Eduardo Leite ( PSD ), nega e atesta equilíbrio nas contas do estado.

O Orçamento para o ano que vem prevê déficit de R$ 4,8 bilhões . O relator da peça orçamentária acredita que o rombo será maior.

O tema ganhou relevância a partir da posição do deputado estadual Gustavo Victorino ( Republicanos ), que foi o mais votado para a Assembleia Legislativa nas eleições de 2022 e neste ano foi eleito deputado federal. O parlamentar afirma que deverá ter atraso de salários no governo Zucco se nada for feito .

"A minha posição é bem clara: é um alerta para as contas públicas que não é de agora. As contas do estado do Rio Grande do Sul estão afundando. Não fiz nada demais, a não ser falar dos números. Temos um déficit primário que não é coberto pelos recursos do estado", afirma Victorino.

O Orçamento para 2027, formulado pelo governo Leite e que tramita no Parlamento gaúcho, prevê déficit fiscal de R$ 4,8 bilhões para o ano que vem.

O deputado Cláudio Branchieri (PL), relator da peça orçamentária na Assembleia e cotado para assumir a Fazenda no governo Zucco, acredita que o saldo negativo possa ser ainda maior, na ordem de R$ 7 bilhões .

"Se eu disser que não há risco (de parcelamento), estaria mentindo. É óbvio que há risco. Eu acredito que nós vamos atrasar salários? Não, não acredito. Mas o risco existe. Ele existe porque as contas públicas estão longe de estar perto da narrativa que o Eduardo Leite quer impor à sociedade gaúcha", declarou Branchieri.

Leite discorda . O governador do Rio Grande do Sul veio a público para rebater as falas dos aliados de Zucco .

"Esses que estão aí dizendo que vai faltar dinheiro foram aqueles que, quando eu disse de onde viria o dinheiro, disseram: não, não queremos o recurso daqui ou dali. E disseram que era possível sustentar as contas do estado fazendo cortes em despesas. Pois agora eles terão a oportunidade de fazer a gestão que eles disseram que dava para fazer", afirmou Leite durante inauguração da nova sede da Polícia Penal.

"Disseram que iam fazer mais, que o estado podia mais, que quer mais, e que bom que ele queira mais. Eu também quero mais para o estado. Pois agora que apresentem os cortes nas despesas possíveis de serem feitos para sustentar sem botar a mão no caixa único . Pois botar a mão do dinheiro do caixa único é arriscar o nosso futuro, quebrar o estado e repetir a receita do passado", declarou em referência à plataforma de campanha eleitoral de Zucco .

O relatório de Branchieri sobre a peça orçamentária para 2027 deve ser apresentado na Assembleia Legislativa nesta segunda-feira (9). Por lei, o Parlamento não pode realizar alterações nas receitas e despesas previstas.

O governo Zucco deve buscar, em Brasília, adiar a volta do pagamento da dívida do estado com a União. As parcelas foram suspensas por três anos após a enchente que atingiu o estado em 2024 e devem voltar a ser cobradas a partir de abril de 2027. O débito gaúcho supera os R$ 100 bilhões.

"Temos de fazer o governo federal aceitar os ativos que o governo do Leite ofereceu e que foram negados, para depois tentar prorrogar o pagamento, porque o Rio Grande do Sul precisa de investimentos urgentes", diz Branchieri.

O governo Leite ofereceu garantias em Brasília por meio de créditos de receitas futuras para se encaixar em uma linha mais vantajosa do Programa de Pleno Pagamento de Dívidas dos Estados (Propag). A Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN) recusou a proposta.

O Rio Grande do Sul tem até abril para aderir ao Propag. Zucco precisará negociar com o governo Lula (PT) para estender a suspensão do pagamento das parcelas.

O Rio Grande do Sul atrasou o pagamento dos salários dos servidores públicos estaduais ao longo de 57 meses , entre os governos José Ivo Sartori ( MDB ) e o primeiro mandato de Leite, então no PSDB .

Em janeiro de 2022, Leite anunciou que o estado pagaria em dia a folha do funcionalismo. Desde então, o Rio Grande do Sul não voltou a atrasar o salário dos funcionários públicos.

articles.title: 10 takeaways from Trump's 60 Minutes interview
articles.summary: Here are the biggest takeaways from our interview with President Trump following bruising GOP midterm losses.
articles.body:
Days after Republicans faced a series of bruising midterm election losses, President Trump stood by his handling of the economy and the Iran war — but he acknowledged some "bad messaging" on economic issues and said his immigration crackdown was "too tough" at times.

In a sitdown with 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat, the president also suggested some top administration officials could be on their way out. One hour later, he announced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles would depart her role and be replaced by Stephen Miller.

Here are the biggest takeaways from the interview:

Republicans lost more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats on Tuesday, with some races still uncalled, including in places that Mr. Trump won by double-digit margins two years ago. About 63% of midterm voters disapproved of Mr. Trump's job performance, and 44% said one reason for their vote was to express opposition to him, according to CBS News exit polling.

Asked for his analysis of the midterm losses, Mr. Trump told 60 Minutes that voters "didn't like the war" with Iran or the soaring gas prices that it triggered.

But he said he believes the primary reason for Republicans' losses was that "I was not on the ballot," an explanation he has offered several times in recent days. He suggested his pre-election endorsements and rallies "brought a lot of people … a lot closer to victory."

Ahead of Election Day, the president frequently urged his supporters to "pretend that I'm on the ballot." So, what happened?

"I think they didn't vote, really. I think they didn't vote. I think in some cases, they didn't like the candidates. And that's, you know, their prerogative," he said.

Some of the candidates were picked by the president. He endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the Lone Star State's bitter GOP Senate primary, and he endorsed Sen. Darline Graham, who was appointed to fill her late brother's South Carolina Senate seat — encouraging her to run for a full term.

Mr. Trump argued that "Cornyn would have lost also."

Economic performance has been "phenomenal," but "we couldn't get the word across"

The president defended his stewardship of the economy in his 60 Minutes sitdown, which came hours after a stronger-than-expected jobs report . He said "the numbers are phenomenal."

"We're doing numbers that have never been done before. 401(k)s are at their all-time high by a lot. Under other presidents, they were a disaster. 401(k)s have made people rich," the president said. Pressed on the fact that not all Americans have large retirement accounts, Mr. Trump responded: "But a lot of people do."

But exit polling shows three-fourths of midterm voters viewed the condition of the economy as either poor or not so good — and 70% of that group voted for Democratic House candidates. Voters were especially concerned about prices of gasoline, food, utilities and healthcare, and two-thirds of voters believed that Mr. Trump's tariff policies hurt the country's economy.

Mr. Trump said the problem is that "we couldn't get the word across."

"I think it was bad messaging, maybe by me, but I would talk about it all the time. So I don't know, how much can I talk about it?" the president said.

He predicted that Americans are "going to notice it in the next two, three, four months," arguing that his policies will lead to a resurgence of manufacturing jobs.

The morning after the election, Vice President JD Vance argued on social media "the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone" — the broadly unpopular Iran war."

Mr. Trump said Vance told him about his plan to write that post, and he responded: "You write what you want." The president said "I don't disagree" with the vice president's diagnosis for why the Republicans lost the midterms, "other than one thing."

"The one thing he left out is — that I would say, and maybe he wouldn't say it, I don't know. I've never asked him really. But, if you had … to do again, would you do it? And that's Iran. Would you go and attack Iran?" he said.

The president said his answer to that question is an "emphatic yes," arguing Iran's conventional military has been degraded and its nuclear program has been set back.

"I think historically, this will be a very good decision. Is it a good decision for today and tomorrow? Maybe not? But … I have to go with what's right for our country," he said. "If they had a nuclear weapon during my term, I would be excoriated far worse than what's happened."

In a visit to the Oval Office later in the day, Mr. Trump reiterated his view that historians will judge the Iran war more favorably than voters. He pointed out a portrait of Ulysses S. Grant, a former president whose reputation has improved with age .

"I mean, he was very low on the list and now he's much higher on the list," Mr. Trump said. "I think as an example — the fact that I have taken the nuclear weapon away from Iran will not be good, short-term. But long-term, I think it's going to be very important."

Since September, Iran and the U.S. have largely held off from major attacks, though the U.S. launched a set of limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets earlier this week.

Mr. Trump has suggested in recent months that the war could ramp up again after the election, but he has also frequently predicted Iran is interested in striking a deal, and Qatar is mediating a diplomatic push between the two sides. He told 60 Minutes he believes Iran is close to striking a deal, but the outcome of the election "gives them a little bit of a hope certificate."

Asked if he plans to escalate the war now that the midterms are over, the president said: "Well, I'm not looking to. I don't think there's any reason to."

On deportation policy, Trump says "I think it was too tough"

Mr. Trump's victory in 2024 was fueled in part by voters' discontent with the Biden administration's immigration policies. But this year, exit polling shows 58% think the Trump administration's actions on immigration have gone too far. In battlegrounds like Texas, many Latino voters who shifted to Mr. Trump two years ago pivoted back to Democrats due to concerns about immigration policy .

The president said immigration "both helped and hurt."

"I think I got an A+ for closing up the border," he said.

So, which immigration policies hurt him?

"For getting people out, I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out," Mr. Trump said. "But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally."

He continued: "Now, there is a large part of the country that think that they should be put out. And there's a large part of the country that think that they should be allowed to stay if they're good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes."

"I think it was too tough," the president said of his deportation policies.

Mr. Trump's plans for the second half of his term aren't clear. On Friday, he replaced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, a hardliner who is widely viewed as an architect of the Trump administration's immigration enforcement strategy. Last year, he pressed Immigration and Customs Enforcement to conduct at least 3,000 arrests per day .

The president said he'd "love to do something on immigration" with congressional Democrats.

"I devote almost no time to my net worth"

Mr. Trump is the wealthiest person to hold the presidency, and his wealth has grown by billions in recent years, fueled partly by his family's cryptocurrency ventures . Polls show many voters believe the president is prioritizing his personal business interests while in office.

Asked about reporting by Forbes that his net worth has soared since he returned to the White House, Mr. Trump said, "So did everyone." (Douthat noted that, unlike Mr. Trump, his net worth hasn't gone up by nearly $3 billion. The president responded, "Well, you should've had stock.")

"I devote almost no time to my net worth. I don't care," he said. "I have a lot of money, and far more than I ever thought I'd have. And I guess it's gone up. I don't even know."

He denied that he is prioritizing his own financial interests, saying his stock holdings are invested in broad indexes and his sons are in charge of his company.

"I have a company. My sons run the company. It's hard to say to them, 'Don't do anything anymore for four years because I'm president," he said.

He also said "every president has had this problem" where people leave the administration to work in private industry, and "no matter what they do, there's a conflict."

Will any administration officials be fired? Trump says he'll "be doing maybe a few changes"

Mr. Trump spoke with 60 Minutes shortly before announcing Wiles' departure. During the interview, he hinted at impending personnel changes .

Asked whether he expected to fire anyone after Republicans' midterm losses, he said: "I do, yeah. Little bit." He added that "I love my Cabinet," but "I'll … be doing maybe a few changes."

Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night, CBS News reported .

CBS News also reported this week that Mr. Trump has asked aides whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should stay in his role. The president told 60 Minutes he has confidence in Hegseth, and pushed back against calls from Democrats to impeach the Pentagon chief.

"They want to impeach him. Very unfair," Mr. Trump said. "We had two wars, we won both. We won Venezuela, we won Iran."

Trump will "probably" endorse a successor, but "not necessarily"

With the 2028 presidential election now two years away, both Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are widely seen as possible heirs to Mr. Trump's political movement. The president has often joked about the succession guessing games.

Asked if he plans to endorse a 2028 Republican primary candidate, Mr. Trump said "probably," but "not necessarily." He said the Republicans "have a tremendous bench" and "I have so many people that I have great relationships with."

Aside from Rubio and Vance, he said "there's some senators that are excellent."

"I may or may not get involved. I don't know," he said. "Maybe I'm better off not getting involved. I think it would play a big role if I did, because my endorsement capacity has been very strong."

Trump planning "tremendous numbers of pardons"

Mr. Trump said he plans to keep using his pardon power aggressively before leaving office.

"I don't want to have good people that are serving this country and doing a great job spending the rest of their life, like I had to do for four years, defending myself by radical left lunatics, by people that were very nasty and mean. I intend to issue tremendous numbers of pardons," he said, joking that "anybody that got within a thousand miles of the Oval Office" could get one.

The president said he doesn't expect to attempt the legally untested maneuver of pardoning himself, but "it's certainly not unreasonable."

He also said: "I pardoned the J6ers. I don't think any group's been treated more unfairly than them, and to this day, when they see me they cry."

Asked about the Jan. 6 rioters who attacked police officers, he argued that "there were some that got rough, but, you know, they were rough to them, too."

Trump on UFOs: Military pilots have "told me things that are very strange"

The president said one of the most frequent questions he gets is about what the military calls unexplained anomalous phenomena — better known as unidentified flying objects, or UFOs.

Earlier this year, Mr. Trump signed an executive order mandating the release of sensitive files on UAP sightings , leading the Pentagon to disclose photos, videos and investigative reports on what appear to be unexplained, often strange objects in the sky.

"I'm not too much of a believer, but I sat in the Oval Office, first term and a little bit second term, meeting with Air Force pilots that are really good, solid people. These are not people that you would say are conspiracy theorists. They don't even know what it means. But they're great, great pilots. Young, handsome. They have beautiful, nice flat tops. I'd like to have a haircut just like them. They look perfect, like Tom Cruise. … They're thin, you know, very thin and very everything. And … they're the real deal. And they've told me things that are very strange."

Toward the end of the sitdown, Douthat asked Mr. Trump — who has survived multiple assassination attempts — what he thinks will happen when he dies.

"Well, I hope I'm missed," he responded.

"Well, I'm a religious person, so in theory, I go to heaven," the president said. "I hope so. I don't want to go to hell."

Douthat asked whether Mr. Trump could forgive his political foes in order to get into heaven.

"The answer is no. I want to be honest, no."

Pressed further, he said the "easy answer" would be to say yes, but he acknowledged: "I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies and always will."
